subject: snail
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module to build a snail at realistic garden snail scale—shell around 3-4 cm diameter, body extending to roughly 6 cm.

For the shell, I'm considering a swept spiral tube with tapering radius versus a lathed dome profile, aiming for something that reads clearly as a coiled snail shell with painted color detailing.

Worried the spiral tube might sink into the dome surface, I'm reconsidering — maybe it's simpler to drop the spiral coil idea entirely and just rely on the lathed shell body with a striped paint pattern instead.

For simplicity I'll skip the explicit whorl geometry and instead suggest the spiral with painted stripe bands around the shell, using the paint function with height and angle coordinates to create a banding pattern that implies coiling. The shell sits upright on the body's back at the hip joint using the default lathe axis.

Now I'm figuring out the body shape for the snail: a tapered form stretching from the head near the front to the tail at the back, sitting flat on the ground with the foot flattened and the body centerline raised slightly. I'm considering whether to build a joint chain with a catmull-rom path for the spine, or just use a single root joint since the body doesn't need complex articulation.

Still defining the skeleton chains...

I'm working out how to reference the tip joint's position for the eye part, then planning the lower tentacles as shorter, simpler sweeps without eyes, parented directly to the head. For the head itself, I'm considering building it as a sweep shape rather than a separate primitive.

Now I'm figuring out the body construction: sweeping tubes along the neck and body chains with radius functions that taper smoothly, overlapping the two sweeps at the junction so seams stay hidden under the rounded caps. I'm thinking through the radius profile to give the mantle its soft, lumpy snail shape while keeping the foot aligned at the bottom.

I'm placing the shell above the body using a lathe profile, checking that its height and width give a realistic garden-snail proportion -- roughly 2.5cm tall, 4cm wide -- positioned so it sinks slightly into the body but overhangs its width for a natural perched look, with a slight tilt for character.

For the shell's coloring, I'm writing a paint function that creates spiral stripes alternating between brown and cream by combining the angular position around the lathe axis with the height, using a fractional wrap to control the spiral density -- settling on roughly 40 bands per meter for a believable pattern, while deciding to skip extra detail like a lighter aperture lip for now.

I'm picking out the full color palette: grayish-beige for the body, a lighter cream for the foot, warm brown for the shell with cream and dark brown spiral paint, near-black for the eyes, and matching tentacle tones. Then I define the shell's lathe profile as a closed outline of coordinates sweeping from the base up to a rounded dome tip, deciding on a light smoothing setting to round the dome while keeping the base corners distinct.

Now I'm planning the foot as a lofted shape bound to the body's bone chain, laying out several stations along the length with varying widths and heights to taper the foot from a rounded front tip through a wider midsection to a tapered tail, checking that each station's bottom edge stays low enough to look grounded. I'm also adjusting the body's vertical radius and center height so it overlaps the foot cleanly without sinking too far below the floor.

Then I'm sketching the body chain as a catmull curve through a few z-positions with a radius function that tapers slightly from front to back, followed by a neck/head chain built the same way, using sweep with shrinking radii to form the head, and figuring out how to grab the head joint as the second joint in that neck chain since a three-point path only yields two joints rather than a separate tip.

Now I'm designing paired eye stalks as small catmull chains rising from the head's top-front, each with two joints plus an eye tip, parented to the head and sized so the base sits within the head's radius; I'm setting the stalk radius profile for the sweep and planning to color it the same as the body.

Next I'm placing a sphere for the eyeball at the stalk's tip, using the tip joint's position, and considering adding a tiny white highlight sphere offset slightly forward and up from the eye to give it some sparkle, while naming the left/right stalks based on the x-direction sign.

I'm sketching the lower tentacles as short sweeps using catmull curves anchored near the head's base, then considering whether to add extra details like a mouth, mantle collar, or shell ridge, but deciding to skip most of these for simplicity. For the shell, I'm placing it via lathe geometry attached to the body chain's second joint, and I'm working out how to set up the root joint so the body chain has a proper parent with no dangling joints.

Now I'm structuring the actual rig code: defining body, neck, and head joints with chain calls, then looping over left/right sides to build stalk chains with eye spheres and highlight dots at their tips, plus the shorter lower tentacles rigidly attached to the head. I'm also writing the lathe outline points and a paint function for the shell's brown-and-cream spiral pattern, checking that the shell's position and size sit naturally on top of the body without clipping awkwardly, and confirming the foot geometry keeps the whole model grounded at y=0 before returning the completed root from the builder.
